STEP 1 - Scene: A Caesar-style salad (chopped romaine lettuce with creamy dressing, croutons, and shaved/grated parmesan) on a white paper plate. Photographed from directly above, so the plate appears roughly circular.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White paper plate, about 23 cm in diameter (roughly a standard small dinner plate). Radius ≈ 11.5 cm, area = 3.14 x 11.5² ≈ 415 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Romaine lettuce pieces, dressed
- Caesar dressing (creamy coating on leaves)
- Croutons
- Shaved parmesan cheese

STEP 4 - Area (share of plate area):
- Romaine lettuce: ~30% (≈125 cm²)
- Caesar dressing (visible on leaves and pooled, counted with lettuce mass): ~5% (≈20 cm²)
- Croutons: ~4% (≈17 cm²)
- Parmesan: ~3% (≈12 cm²)
Total food coverage ≈ 42% of the plate, which is a loose, partial pile.

STEP 5 - Volume (height estimates):
- Lettuce: 125 cm² x 2.5 cm ≈ 312 ml
- Dressing: 20 cm² x 0.3 cm ≈ 6 ml
- Croutons: 17 cm² x 1 cm ≈ 17 ml
- Parmesan: 12 cm² x 0.3 cm ≈ 4 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Lettuce: 312 ml x 0.15 ≈ 47 g
- Dressing: 6 ml x 1.0 ≈ 6 g (Caesar dressing is oil-based, so this is a light estimate; the dressing is largely clinging to the leaves)
- Croutons: 17 ml x 0.3 (bread-like, airy) ≈ 5 g
- Parmesan: 4 ml x 1.0 ≈ 4 g
Total ≈ 62 g.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Romaine lettuce, dressed: 47 g x 20 kcal/100 g ≈ 9 kcal (dressing counted separately)
- Caesar dressing: 6 g x 470 kcal/100 g ≈ 28 kcal
- Croutons: 5 g x 400 kcal/100 g ≈ 20 kcal
- Parmesan: 4 g x 420 kcal/100 g ≈ 17 kcal
Total ≈ 74 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A visible salad covering under half a paper plate with a light coating of dressing, croutons, and cheese, around 60 g and roughly 75 kcal, is plausible. The dressing may be somewhat under-counted, since creamy Caesar often adds more fat than it looks, so the energy could be somewhat higher.
